caption: The drawing features a single object depicted in three different views: a perspective view, a top view, and a side elevation, all rendered in grayscale pencil or ink. The object itself appears to be a flat, perforated artifact with an ornate, symmetrical openwork design, possibly made of metal. Its overall shape resembles a teardrop or leaf, with one pointed end and a rounded handle-like extension at the opposite end, which contains a circular hole and two smaller oval holes. The central portion contains interwoven geometric and curvilinear patterns, with multiple negative spaces formed by the openwork. In the top left corner of the drawing, the object is shown from above, clearly displaying the symmetrical openwork design. Directly below this top view, a thin side elevation view shows the flat profile of the object, supported by two short legs. Beneath the side elevation is a linear scale marked from 0 to 3, likely representing centimeters. The largest image, occupying the lower right area, is a three-quarter perspective view illustrating the depth, thickness, and dimensionality of the object, with careful shading to indicate its metallic appearance and the form of the openwork. The background is plain, and the drawing is surrounded by a thin rectangular border.
title: Flat Iron Holder
